description: Pipe/tube resonances. To author a tube body, place a resonance at each partial frequency. The partials are a HARMONIC series (open-open) or ODD harmonics only (closed-open). Tubes ring, so radii are high (narrow bandwidth). The natural morph for a tube is LENGTH: shorten the tube and the whole series scales up together (all poles slide in lock-step) — that's a uniform scale, not a formant crossing.

physics.open_open: both ends open (flute-like): f_n = n * c / (2L),  n = 1,2,3,... (full harmonic series)
physics.closed_open: one end closed (clarinet-like): f_n = (2n-1) * c / (4L),  n = 1,2,3,... (odd harmonics only; sounds an octave lower and hollow)
physics.end_correction: effective length L_eff = L + 0.6*radius per open end; ignore for a first pass

q_guidance.note: Metal/glass tubes ring hard = narrow bandwidth = high radius. Plastic/cardboard are more damped. Bandwidth narrows (radius rises) with the Q axis.

morph_guidance: Tube length = the headline morph. Pick two lengths (M0 long/low, M100 short/high); every partial scales by the same ratio. The Q axis = damping/ring (broad -> sharp). This is the SCALE morph type, distinct from the vowel anchors+crossers template.

morph_pairs.name: long -> short (open)
morph_pairs.motion: all harmonics scale up ~5x together — a pitch/length sweep

morph_pairs.name: open -> stopped
morph_pairs.motion: even harmonics fade as the tube goes hollow/odd-only
